mergedParams.userDescription: Subtle scale pop and ease. internal effects for text, video, images

output.title: Subtle Scale Pop & Ease Internal Effects

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'subtle-pop' that provides a gentle scale animation with smooth easing for text, video, and image elements. The effect should scale from 0.95 to 1.02 and back to 1.0, creating a subtle 'pop' that draws attention without being jarring. Use a spring easing function for organic motion. Accept parameters for duration (default 0.4s), intensity (scale multiplier, default 1.0), and delay (default 0). The effect should use provider mode targeting components by ID. Return a generic effect with AnimationRange keyframes at prog 0 (scale 0.95), 0.4 (scale 1.02), and 1.0 (scale 1.0). Think like a motion designer creating micro-interactions that feel responsive but not overwhelming.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange. Properties: scale with spring easing. Input schema: z.object({ duration: z.number().default(0.4), intensity: z.number().default(1.0), delay: z.number().default(0), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). AnimationRange: [{ key: 'scale', val: 0.95 * intensity, prog: 0 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1.02 * intensity, prog: 0.4 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1.0, prog: 1 }]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: delay, duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'spring' }. PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset named 'ease-in-scale' that creates a smooth scale-in animation perfect for revealing content. Start from scale 0.8 with opacity 0, then ease into full scale 1.0 with opacity 1. Use ease-out easing for a decelerating curve that feels natural. Support parameters for startScale (0.7-0.95), duration (0.3-2s), and optional blur effect (0-10px at start). The effect should combine scale and opacity animations in a single generic effect. Target multiple elements simultaneously using targetIds array. Think of this as a video editor's go-to transition for introducing new elements on screen.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange with combined properties. Properties: scale, opacity, optional blur. Input schema: z.object({ startScale: z.number().min(0.7).max(0.95).default(0.8), duration: z.number().default(0.5), withBlur: z.boolean().default(false), blurAmount: z.number().default(5), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). AnimationRange: [{ key: 'scale', val: startScale, prog: 0 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 1 }, { key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 0 }, { key: 'opacity', val: 1, prog: 1 }, ...withBlur ? [{ key: 'blur', val: blurAmount, prog: 0 }, { key: 'blur', val: 0, prog: 1 }] : []]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'ease-out' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'audio-pulse' that creates audio-reactive scale pulsing synchronized with bass beats. The effect should analyze bass frequencies and apply subtle scale changes (0.98-1.04) that match the rhythm. Include sensitivity control (0.1-1.0) and threshold settings to filter out weak beats. Support different pulse modes: 'smooth' (continuous scaling) or 'punchy' (quick scale pops). Perfect for making text or images respond to music. Think like a VJ creating real-time visual reactions to audio, but subtle enough for professional use.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: waveform (audio-reactive). Waveform config: { type: 'scale', audio: 'bass', sensitivity: 0.5-1.0, threshold: 0.3, smoothing: mode === 'smooth' ? 0.8 : 0.2 }. Input schema: z.object({ sensitivity: z.number().min(0.1).max(1.0).default(0.5), threshold: z.number().default(0.3), mode: z.enum(['smooth', 'punchy']).default('smooth'), minScale: z.number().default(0.98), maxScale: z.number().default(1.04), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Effect data: { type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: 'parent', mode: 'provider', targetIds, props: { type: 'scale', audio: 'bass', sensitivity, threshold, min: minScale, max: maxScale, smoothing } }. PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset named 'breath-scale' that simulates organic breathing motion through scale animation. Use a sine-wave-like progression with multiple cycles to create a rhythmic in-and-out scaling effect. Scale oscillates between 0.97 and 1.03 with customizable breathing rate (cycles per duration). Include phase offset parameter to desynchronize multiple elements. Perfect for creating living, organic motion in UI elements. Think of this as adding life to static elements, like a filmmaker uses subtle camera movement to keep scenes dynamic.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange with calculated sine wave keyframes. Properties: scale with custom sine interpolation. Input schema: z.object({ cycles: z.number().default(2), amplitude: z.number().default(0.03), duration: z.number().default(3), phaseOffset: z.number().default(0), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). AnimationRange generation: Create 20 keyframes using: Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => { const prog = i / 19; const val = 1 + amplitude * Math.sin((prog * cycles + phaseOffset) * Math.PI * 2); return { key: 'scale', val, prog }; }). Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'linear' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset called 'elastic-pop' that creates a bouncy, elastic scale animation inspired by cartoon physics. Start at rest (scale 1.0), compress slightly (0.92), then overshoot target (1.12), oscillate with decreasing amplitude, and settle at 1.0. Include tension and friction parameters to control the elastic behavior. Support both scale and optional rotation for playful motion. Think like an animator creating exaggerated but appealing motion that adds personality to elements.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange with elastic overshoot. Properties: scale, optional rotate. Input schema: z.object({ tension: z.number().default(0.8), friction: z.number().default(0.3), overshoot: z.number().default(0.12), withRotation: z.boolean().default(false), maxRotation: z.number().default(5), duration: z.number().default(0.8), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). AnimationRange: [{ key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 0 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1 - overshoot * 0.75, prog: 0.15 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1 + overshoot, prog: 0.35 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1 - overshoot * 0.3, prog: 0.55 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1 + overshoot * 0.15, prog: 0.75 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 1 }, ...withRotation ? elastic rotation keyframes : []]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'ease-out' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset named 'focus-pop' that combines scale with blur and brightness adjustments to create a focusing effect. Start slightly blurred and dimmed at scale 0.96, then pop to sharp focus with scale 1.02 and slight brightness boost, before settling to normal. Include depth-of-field simulation with customizable blur radius. Perfect for drawing attention to hero elements. Think like a cinematographer using focus pulls and exposure adjustments to guide viewer attention.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange with multiple properties. Properties: scale, blur, brightness. Input schema: z.object({ initialBlur: z.number().default(3), peakScale: z.number().default(1.02), brightBoost: z.number().default(1.1), duration: z.number().default(0.6), holdDuration: z.number().default(0.1), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). AnimationRange: [{ key: 'scale', val: 0.96, prog: 0 }, { key: 'scale', val: peakScale, prog: 0.4 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 1 }, { key: 'blur', val: initialBlur, prog: 0 }, { key: 'blur', val: 0, prog: 0.3 }, { key: 'brightness', val: 0.9, prog: 0 }, { key: 'brightness', val: brightBoost, prog: 0.4 }, { key: 'brightness', val: 1, prog: 1 }]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'ease-in-out' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'heartbeat' that mimics a heartbeat rhythm with two quick scale pulses followed by a pause. First pulse to 1.05, quick dip to 0.98, second stronger pulse to 1.08, then rest at 1.0. Support BPM parameter to sync with actual heart rates (60-180 BPM). Include intensity multiplier and optional opacity pulse. Think of medical monitors and fitness apps - create that recognizable double-beat pattern that signals life and energy.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange with heartbeat pattern. Properties: scale, optional opacity. Input schema: z.object({ bpm: z.number().min(60).max(180).default(72), intensity: z.number().default(1.0), withOpacityPulse: z.boolean().default(false), loop: z.boolean().default(true), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Calculate beat duration: 60/bpm seconds. AnimationRange: [{ key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 0 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1.05 * intensity, prog: 0.1 }, { key: 'scale', val: 0.98, prog: 0.15 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1.08 * intensity, prog: 0.25 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 0.4 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 1 }, ...withOpacityPulse ? opacity keyframes : []]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: 60/bpm, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'ease-out', loop }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset named 'magnetic-snap' that creates a magnetic attraction effect where elements appear to be pulled then snap into place. Start with slow acceleration (scale 0.94), build momentum, then snap quickly to slight overshoot (1.04) before settling. Include magnetic 'strength' parameter affecting acceleration curve. Add optional slight rotation wobble for more dynamic motion. Think like a UI animator creating satisfying interactions that feel physical and responsive.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange with magnetic acceleration curve. Properties: scale, optional rotate for wobble. Input schema: z.object({ magnetStrength: z.number().min(0.1).max(2.0).default(1.0), overshoot: z.number().default(0.04), wobble: z.boolean().default(false), wobbleAmount: z.number().default(2), duration: z.number().default(0.5), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). AnimationRange: [{ key: 'scale', val: 0.94, prog: 0 }, { key: 'scale', val: 0.93, prog: 0.2 * magnetStrength }, { key: 'scale', val: 0.95, prog: 0.5 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1 + overshoot, prog: 0.75 }, { key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 1 }, ...wobble ? [{ key: 'rotate', val: -wobbleAmount, prog: 0.7 }, { key: 'rotate', val: wobbleAmount * 0.5, prog: 0.85 }, { key: 'rotate', val: 0, prog: 1 }] : []]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'ease-in-out' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'frequency-scale' that creates scale reactions based on specific frequency ranges in audio. Allow targeting bass, mid, or treble frequencies with different scale responses. Include frequency isolation to react only to specific instruments or vocals. Support smooth vs stepped scaling modes. Perfect for music visualizers or presentations synced to audio. Think like an audio engineer visualizing different frequency bands through motion.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: waveform (audio-reactive) with frequency targeting. Waveform config: { type: 'scale', audio: frequencyBand, sensitivity, threshold, smoothing }. Input schema: z.object({ frequencyBand: z.enum(['bass', 'mid', 'treble', 'full']).default('bass'), sensitivity: z.number().default(0.6), threshold: z.number().default(0.25), minScale: z.number().default(0.95), maxScale: z.number().default(1.05), smoothing: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.5), isolate: z.boolean().default(false), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Effect data: { type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: 'parent', mode: 'provider', targetIds, props: { type: 'scale', audio: frequencyBand, sensitivity, threshold, min: minScale, max: maxScale, smoothing, isolate } }. PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset named 'gentle-float' that combines subtle scale oscillation with slight Y-axis translation to create a floating effect. Scale varies between 0.98-1.02 while translateY moves -2px to 2px in a offset sine pattern. Include parameters for float speed, amplitude, and whether to include slight rotation sway. Perfect for creating ambient motion in backgrounds or idle states. Think like a motion designer adding secondary animation to keep scenes alive without distraction.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic AnimationRange with combined scale and translate. Properties: scale, translateY, optional rotate. Input schema: z.object({ floatSpeed: z.number().default(4), scaleAmplitude: z.number().default(0.02), translateAmplitude: z.number().default(2), withSway: z.boolean().default(false), swayAmount: z.number().default(1), duration: z.number().default(4), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). AnimationRange generation: Create keyframes with offset sine waves: Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_, i) => { const prog = i / 15; const scaleVal = 1 + scaleAmplitude * Math.sin(prog * Math.PI * 2); const translateVal = translateAmplitude * Math.sin((prog + 0.25) * Math.PI * 2); return [{ key: 'scale', val: scaleVal, prog }, { key: 'translateY', val: translateVal, prog }]; }).flat(). Add rotation if withSway. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges, easing: 'linear', loop: true }. Return: { effects: [effectData] }
